done_when: forge close's test runs on one machine go strictly in the order they started waiting (first come, first served), and a waiting close prints its place in line when it starts waiting and each time the place changes, as one plain line such as 'Waiting for 3 other closes' test runs on this machine.' A close that dies leaves no stale place. A command-level test starts three waiting closes behind a held run and shows they run in arrival order and print their places.
why: About twenty closes share the machine's one test-run lock; a waiting close can be overtaken again and again and never says how long it will wait
